lines.display: On *1* *April* *1929*, Matsuzakaya's rebuilt Ueno store
lines.spoken: On the first of April, nineteen twenty-nine, Mah-tsoo-zah-ka-ya's rebuilt Oo-eh-no store

lines.display: opened in Tokyo with something *new*: women running the *elevators*.
lines.spoken: opened in Tokyo with something new: women running the elevators.

lines.display: People called them *“shōkōki* *girls”*: lift girls.
lines.spoken: People called them show-koh-kee girls: lift girls.

lines.display: Matsuzakaya calls them Japan's *first*.
lines.spoken: Mah-tsoo-zah-ka-ya calls them Japan's first.

lines.display: One history says *Kobe* got there *earlier*, at Daimaru,
lines.spoken: One history says Koh-beh got there earlier, at Dye-mah-roo,

lines.display: where men rode up a *single* *floor* just to see them.
lines.spoken: where men rode up a single floor just to see them.

lines.display: Ueno hired *seven* *or* *eight* women aged *18* and over.
lines.spoken: Oo-eh-no hired seven or eight women aged eighteen and over.

lines.display: Its elevators were driven by turning a *handle*,
lines.spoken: Its elevators were driven by turning a handle,

lines.display: so they *steered* and *called* *out* *floors* at once.
lines.spoken: so they steered and called out floors at once.

lines.display: Beginners sometimes stopped a *foot* off the floor.
lines.spoken: Beginners sometimes stopped a foot off the floor.

lines.display: Service work then ranked *below* desk jobs,
lines.spoken: Service work then ranked below desk jobs,

lines.display: but some saw these women as *modern* *professionals*,
lines.spoken: but some saw these women as modern professionals,

lines.display: and after the war the job's standing *rose*.
lines.spoken: and after the war the job's standing rose.

lines.display: Postwar, they spread to office towers and *Tokyo* *Tower*,
lines.spoken: Postwar, they spread to office towers and Tokyo Tower,

lines.display: where one might ride up and down *12* *or* *13* times in half an hour.
lines.spoken: where one might ride up and down twelve or thirteen times in half an hour.

lines.display: *Sore* *legs*, *stiff* *shoulders*, *pushy* *customers* —
lines.spoken: Sore legs, stiff shoulders, pushy customers —

lines.display: yet it was an *admired* city job.
lines.spoken: yet it was an admired city job.

lines.display: In the slump of the *1990s*, most stores switched to *automatic* lifts.
lines.spoken: In the slump of the nineteen nineties, most stores switched to automatic lifts.

lines.display: But at Nihombashi Takashimaya, attendants *still* *drive* Otis cars from *1933*,
lines.spoken: But at Nee-hom-bah-shee Tah-kah-shee-mah-ya, attendants still drive Otis cars from nineteen thirty-three,

lines.display: and Matsuzakaya Ueno still rides its original *1929* lifts, *automated* now.
lines.spoken: and Mah-tsoo-zah-ka-ya Oo-eh-no still rides its original nineteen twenty-nine lifts, automated now.

lines.spoken: Next: a nineteen thirty-two fire at Shee-ro-kee-ya,

lines.display: and the famous story that it changed what women wore under their kimono.
lines.spoken: and the famous story that it changed what women wore under their kimono.
